# Evolution

How a campaign changes the harness that runs it, Crustify's skills, agents, templates and
providers, its tools and the tools it lacks, and how its agents propose changes to the
campaign's artifacts that other roles own. A campaign exposes what the harness gets
wrong, what it constrains needlessly and what it repeats by hand; evolution turns that
evidence into changes, under the autonomy the settings' `evolution` answer grants, and
this guidance itself among them. Where a change goes within Crustify is
[`authoring`](../authoring/SKILL.md)'s.

## 1. Goals

Every change is judged against Crustify's goals, [`GOALS.md`](../../../GOALS.md), read in
full before the first proposal: a change serves one of them, or it is not made. The goals
are evolved too, when the evidence questions them, as `GOALS.md` describes.

A change to a tool is judged against that tool's own goals and non-goals too, the document
its tool skill names, read in full before the first change to the tool: they keep what the
tool is from drifting, such as an analysis that stays syntactic and does no data-flow
analysis. A change that departs from one of them is proposed, not made, and says so. A
tool with no such document has every change that alters what it is, rather than fixing or
extending what it does, proposed, not made.
<!-- TODO: ffimap has no goals document yet. -->

## 2. Signals

Evolution starts from evidence a campaign produces, never from taste:

| signal | what it suggests |
|---|---|
| a tool that crashes, or reports what the source contradicts | a defect in the tool |
| skills that contradict each other, or an agent prompt that leads its agent wrong | a defect in the spec |
| a rule an agent works around, or that forces a worse result than its omission would | an overconstraining rule, loosened or removed |
| review findings that recur across batches, in one objective or category | a rule the how-to skills lack |
| failed or rerun batches, and plan corrections | a defect in planning, scheduling or packing |
| the user's corrections | a rule, or a lesson of the campaign |
| cost or time outliers, in the dashboard | waste in batch sizing, gates or tooling |
| one representation hand-written in several places, or a TODO met again and again | a primitive or tool feature that is missing |
| one procedure repeated by hand: the same script written again, the same queries run in sequence | a tool, or a subcommand of one |
| a signal evolution missed, or a proposal that proved wrong | a defect in this guidance |
| a goal no decision cites, two that keep conflicting the same way, or a well-founded change no goal serves | a change to the goals |

A proposal needs one of these, with its evidence: a defect, a failure, a recurring
finding, a workaround or a measured waste. Fewer, well-founded proposals serve better than
many small ones: a change made for style alone, or for completeness, or to have proposed
something, is not made.

## 3. Destinations

Each signal goes to one destination:

- **the campaign alone**: what a setting or a task message settles, which changes nothing
  of Crustify;
- **a lesson**: a rule that holds for this target alone, recorded in the campaign's
  [`LESSONS.md`](#5-lessons);
- **the spec**: a skill, an agent, a template or a provider, where `authoring` places it;
- **a tool**: its code, its documentation or its tests, or a new tool; or
- **a campaign artifact**: the plan, the dependencies, the schedule or the dashboard, where
  the evidence shows one wrong or improvable and another role owns it. Its owner applies
  the proposal or declines it, a plan's at the next planner run.

A rule an agent cannot follow because its host refuses it, a write or a tool call
blocked, or a launch mode that withholds what the role needs, is a defect of that host's
provider, not of the rule: the provider prevents it with whatever its host offers, its
agents' definitions, the settings and permissions it installs, its hooks, the mode it
launches runs in, or the host's memory, and the spec is not bent around one host. Until
the provider's change lands, a run that meets the refusal neither works around it nor drops
what it could not do: it hands that to the assistant, in its final message, and the
assistant carries it out.

The test between a lesson and the spec is generality: a rule that can only be stated in
the target's own names is a lesson, and one the spec takes is stated without them, as it
would hold for any C codebase.

## 4. Proposals

A proposal is filed in the campaign's repository under `crustify/evolution/<slug>/`, as its
`PROPOSAL.md`. It states:

- the signal and its evidence, with the runs, findings and commits it cites;
- the goal it serves, by name, and the fitness measure of that goal it expects to move;
- its destination;
- the change, or the patch;
- how it was validated;
- the row the record takes when the change lands, as [`evolution-record`](record/SKILL.md) describes;

evidence into changes, under the autonomy the settings' `evolution` answer grants, and
this guidance itself among them. Where a change goes within Crustify is
[`authoring`](../authoring/SKILL.md)'s.

## 1. Goals

Every change is judged against Crustify's goals, [`GOALS.md`](../../../GOALS.md), read in
full before the first proposal: a change serves one of them, or it is not made. The goals
are evolved too, when the evidence questions them, as `GOALS.md` describes.

A change to a tool is judged against that tool's own goals and non-goals too, the document
its tool skill names, read in full before the first change to the tool: they keep what the
tool is from drifting, such as an analysis that stays syntactic and does no data-flow
analysis. A change that departs from one of them is proposed, not made, and says so. A
tool with no such document has every change that alters what it is, rather than fixing or
extending what it does, proposed, not made.
<!-- TODO: ffimap has no goals document yet. -->

## 2. Signals

Evolution starts from evidence a campaign produces, never from taste:

| signal | what it suggests |
|---|---|
| a tool that crashes, or reports what the source contradicts | a defect in the tool |
| skills that contradict each other, or an agent prompt that leads its agent wrong | a defect in the spec |
| a rule an agent works around, or that forces a worse result than its omission would | an overconstraining rule, loosened or removed |
| review findings that recur across batches, in one objective or category | a rule the how-to skills lack |
| failed or rerun batches, and plan corrections | a defect in planning, scheduling or packing |
| the user's corrections | a rule, or a lesson of the campaign |
| cost or time outliers, in the dashboard | waste in batch sizing, gates or tooling |
| one representation hand-written in several places, or a TODO met again and again | a primitive or tool feature that is missing |
| one procedure repeated by hand: the same script written again, the same queries run in sequence | a tool, or a subcommand of one |
| a signal evolution missed, or a proposal that proved wrong | a defect in this guidance |
| a goal no decision cites, two that keep conflicting the same way, or a well-founded change no goal serves | a change to the goals |

A proposal needs one of these, with its evidence: a defect, a failure, a recurring
finding, a workaround or a measured waste. Fewer, well-founded proposals serve better than
many small ones: a change made for style alone, or for completeness, or to have proposed
something, is not made.

## 3. Destinations

Each signal goes to one destination:

- **the campaign alone**: what a setting or a task message settles, which changes nothing
  of Crustify;
- **a lesson**: a rule that holds for this target alone, recorded in the campaign's
  [`LESSONS.md`](#5-lessons);
- **the spec**: a skill, an agent, a template or a provider, where `authoring` places it;
- **a tool**: its code, its documentation or its tests, or a new tool; or
- **a campaign artifact**: the plan, the dependencies, the schedule or the dashboard, where
  the evidence shows one wrong or improvable and another role owns it. Its owner applies
  the proposal or declines it, a plan's at the next planner run.

A rule an agent cannot follow because its host refuses it, a write or a tool call
blocked, or a launch mode that withholds what the role needs, is a defect of that host's
provider, not of the rule: the provider prevents it with whatever its host offers, its
agents' definitions, the settings and permissions it installs, its hooks, the mode it
launches runs in, or the host's memory, and the spec is not bent around one host. Until
the provider's change lands, a run that meets the refusal neither works around it nor drops
what it could not do: it hands that to the assistant, in its final message, and the
assistant carries it out.

The test between a lesson and the spec is generality: a rule that can only be stated in
the target's own names is a lesson, and one the spec takes is stated without them, as it
would hold for any C codebase.

## 4. Proposals

A proposal is filed in the campaign's repository under `crustify/evolution/<slug>/`, as its
`PROPOSAL.md`. It states:

- the signal and its evidence, with the runs, findings and commits it cites;
- the goal it serves, by name, and the fitness measure of that goal it expects to move;
- its destination;
- the change, or the patch;
- how it was validated;
- the row the record takes when the change lands, as [`evolution-record`](record/SKILL.md) describes;

# Goals

This file states what Crustify is for and how it evolves. Every change to Crustify is judged
against these goals, whether it changes its skills, its agents or its tools.

A rule that serves none of these goals is removed. Where two goals are in tension, they are
weighed for the case at hand, and the weighing is stated.

The goals evolve too, from the same evidence as everything else:

- a goal the campaigns keep missing;
- a goal no decision ever cites;
- two goals that keep conflicting the same way; or
- a well-founded change that none of the goals serves.

A change to the goals is proposed as Crustify's `evolution` skill describes. It lands only
with the user's approval.

Each goal names its *fitness*: what a campaign measures to tell how far the goal is met. Each
thing measured is a *measure*. A measure is read from one of two sources, and no run is made
only to take it:

- what the campaign's runs produce anyway: the dashboard, the review reports, the gates and
  the plan; or
- a rerun the campaign's reviews already make.

A *tier* is one of the checks that code meets one after another. An *escape* is a defect
caught by a later tier than the one that read the code first. Later tiers include:

- a module pass after a wave's review;
- a switch;
- a revisit; and
- a ship point's gates.

Worse work could improve some measures. Such a measure is *paired* with the measure that
catches the worse work, which is its *pair*, and neither is read alone. When there are more
escapes, fewer findings is no gain. When the work is redone, cheaper work is no gain.

Some measures are held by no artifact yet. Such a measure is marked **Not taken yet**. Until
it is taken, what it measures is judged, not measured.

Under each goal, **Measure** states a measure, **Paired with** names its pair, and **Not
taken yet** names what no artifact holds yet.

## 1. Safety

No undefined behaviour is reachable from safe Rust. The unsafe code that remains sits in its
regions, and is sound for every input.

### The unsafe surface

- **Measure.** What a deterministic scan counts on each landing:
  - raw pointers and `unsafe fn`s on the public API;
  - unsafe lines and raw dereferences; and
  - unsafe code outside its regions.

  The first two fall as a module goes from wrapped to ported and through its later stages.
  The third is zero throughout.
- **Paired with** soundness, below. Calling an unsound function safe takes an obligation off
  the API, and so lowers this measure.

### Soundness

- **Measure.** The defects a reproducer proves, as the review reports file them by kind.
  These defects are undefined behaviour and contracts that can be broken.
- **Paired with** the escapes among these defects.
- **Not taken yet.** The tier that caught a defect. Also the unsafe sites a review read,
  which the defects are counted against.

## 2. Equivalence

The Rust keeps the C's specified behaviour, not its bugs. The specified behaviour is what
the C's documentation, tests and consumers rely on.

- **Measure.**
  - The target's own tests passing over the Rust at each switch, against their recorded
    baseline.
  - The inputs and states on which the Rust is compared with the C it replaces, with no
    difference left unexplained.
  - The differences made on purpose, each documented and held by a test.
- **Paired with** the differences found after the comparison ended. They are found by a
  review, at a switch, or by a consumer.
- **Not taken yet.** The inputs compared and the deliberate differences, as figures. Each
  run's notes alone hold them.

## 3. Idiomatic Rust

The API a Rust consumer sees is native Rust: ownership, borrowing, errors, iteration and
traits. It is not C's conventions behind a Rust syntax.

- **Measure.** The C forms that Safety's scan still counts on the public API: raw and
  untyped pointers, and obligations handed to callers. Also the ergonomics and idiom
  findings that reviews file, counted per item reviewed.
- **Paired with** the ergonomics and idiom findings that a later tier or a consumer makes on
  an item an earlier review passed. A review that reads less finds less.
- **Not taken yet.** Which tier made a finding.

## 4. Performance

The emitted Rust costs no more than native Rust would. Where tokens and time buy
accuracy, the harness spends them.

### The harness

- **Measure.** Cost and wall time per translated item, reviews and switches included.
- **Paired with** what was redone: batches run again, gates rerun and merges made twice.
- **Paired with** Safety's and Equivalence's measures: cheaper work with more escapes is not
  cheaper.

### The emitted Rust

- **Measure.** The emitted Rust's time and memory against the C it replaces, on the target's
  own workloads.
- **Paired with** Safety's and Equivalence's measures, since a check dropped is time saved.
- **Not taken yet.** The whole measure.
  <!-- TODO: no campaign benchmarks what it ports; which workloads, and at which event,
  is not specified. -->

## 5. Verification

content.content:
What the agents produce is machine-checked wherever it can be, rather than left to an
agent's judgement. It is checked by types, lints, sanitizers, Miri, schemas, deterministic
tools and compile-time assertions.

- **Measure.** The line coverage of the ported Rust.
- **Paired with** the share of deliberate faults that the ported Rust's tests catch, since
  code that runs is not code that is checked.
- **Paired with** the gate results that a run reported and that its landed tree does not
  reproduce. A review files these gate results among its reports.
- **Not taken yet.**
  - the seeded faults, which are taken only where a review happens to seed them;
  - the region coverage of the ported Rust; and
  - the states and transitions the tests reach.
  <!-- TODO: seeding faults is not a step of any stage yet. -->

## 6. Maintainability

Established software engineering practice and reuse keep the emitted Rust and the harness
itself maintainable for the long term. Each rule and each piece of code has one place.
Standard libraries and idioms come before new ones.

- **Measure.** What was reused against what was made again:
  - owners, callbacks and lifecycles built from the shared primitives rather than by hand, as
    Safety's scan counts them; and
  - library entities reached through the standard library or an adopted crate rather than a
    new binding, as the plan records each one's route.

  A procedure worked out by hand a second time, and a proposal that repeats another's signal,
  count against this measure.
- **Paired with** Least constraint's measure. Where a rule forces reuse and what is reused
  does not fit, that reuse is counted there.

## 7. Interoperability

C and Rust work together soundly in both directions for as long as both remain. Each reaches
the other through the boundary in its own conventions. The Rust also works with the Rust
ecosystem: the standard library's types and traits, and existing crates where they serve.

- **Measure.**
  - The remaining C's tests passing over the Rust link.
  - The build modes and variants the crate builds and tests in.
  - The kinds of crossing a campaign exercises and passes, in each direction:
    - exports checked against the C declarations they replace;
    - callbacks C makes into Rust and Rust into C; and
    - layouts and storage the remaining C shares.
- **Not taken yet.** The kinds of crossing, as a count.

## 8. Incremental migration without breaking consumers

A codebase moves to Rust one module at a time. Every landing builds and passes its gates. No
consumer breaks: a C or Rust consumer's code does not change as what it consumes is wrapped,
ported or moves through its later stages.

- **Measure.**
  - The items whose API changed or went after their first landing, each with its reason.
  - The landed trees that failed a gate.
  - The target's test baseline, which moves only by the cases carried over.
- **Paired with** Idiomatic Rust's measure of C forms on the public API. An API that never
  changes because it stayed C's breaks no one and serves no one.

### The order

- **Measure.** The batches that met a dependency not yet landed, and waited for it, rewrote
  around it or reached past its wrapper.

  Items land after what they depend on. Where the order cuts a cycle, an item lands after
  the binding of what it depends on. That order is how this goal is met, and Safety's and
  Performance's with it: a consumer written once, over a boundary written once.
- **Not taken yet.** The whole measure.

## 9. Generality

The rules hold for any C codebase. What holds for one target alone is that target's lesson,
not a rule.

- **Measure.** Of what a campaign's evidence taught, the share stated as rules without the
  target's names against the share kept as the target's lessons. Also the rules a second
  target could not follow as written.

## 10. Least constraint

A rule states what must hold. Unless the how is itself what must hold, the rule leaves the
how to the agent.

- **Measure.** Per module, the rules that a run:
  - worked around;
  - rewrote sound code to satisfy; or
  - reported as forcing a worse result.
- **Paired with** what a loosened rule let through: the changes marked as weakening a check,
  and the defects found where a rule was loosened.

## 11. Consistency

One kind of item is translated one way. Items that mean the same in C take the same Rust
pattern, whatever their syntax and whichever agent, batch or campaign translates them. The
pattern is the one the conventions and the how-to skills give them. A departure states its
reason.

A pattern a skill gives is a how that must hold, in Least constraint's terms. A pattern is
given only where translating the same thing two ways costs a consumer or a reviewer. Where
the skills give none, the agent chooses. A choice met twice, where two ways would cost, is
proposed as the pattern rather than left to converge.

- **Measure.** The conventions findings reviews file, per item.
- **Paired with** two measures, since a review that reads less finds less:
  - the items a later batch or review reshaped; and
  - the conventions findings a later tier makes on an item an earlier review passed.
- **Not taken yet.**
  - both paired measures;
  - the departures that state their reason, against the departures a review had to find; and
  - whether an item translated twice took the same shape both times.

## 12. Attribution

Every fact a decision rests on can be reproduced. Every change traces back to the run, and
the revisions, that made it.

- **Measure.** The landed commits, dashboard cells and decisions that trace to a run, its
  session and its revisions, against those that do not. Two examples of those that do not: a
  run without a recorded session, and a figure no rerun of its tool reproduces.
## 1. Record

Every change that lands is recorded in Crustify's own repository, in
[`EVOLUTION.md`](../../../../EVOLUTION.md), whatever component it changed, so that a later
campaign can tell whether it held. A row gives the campaign and proposal the change came
from, the component and commit it landed as, the signal it answered, its recurrence signal
and its status, with a change that weakens a check marked so in its status. A change no
proposal filed names its campaign and `no proposal` in its place, with where it came from.
A proposal that lands several changes takes a row for each.

A change's row is drafted in its proposal, so that the review reads it. The record's writer
copies the row into the record when the change lands. An evolution branch never edits
`EVOLUTION.md`, so that two changes awaiting review never conflict there, and the record
has one writer per campaign. The record holds every change landed since it began, on
2026-11-12; what landed before is not recorded.

The recurrence signal is what a campaign would observe if the issue were back, in what a
campaign produces anyway: a review finding of a category, a run that fails for a cause, a
tool's error, a correction the user repeats. A change whose regression test checks all of
it has `test` in its place and is not watched. One with no signal a campaign could observe
has `none`, with why, and is not watched either.

A watched change is:

- `watched` from its landing;
- `recurred` once its signal is met again, with the evidence, which opens a proposal that
  cites the row: the change was wrong or partial, or the validation and review that passed
  it were; and
- `confirmed` once a campaign other than the one it came from has ended, having exercised
  it, without the signal.

A row's signal is looked for at two times, in every campaign:

- when a proposal is indexed, as [`evolution`](../SKILL.md)'s Proposals section describes:
  a signal that matches a row's recurrence signal marks that row `recurred`; and
- periodically, when the rows still `watched` are read against the findings, failed runs,
  proposals and corrections since the last reading. The campaign sets the period from its
  state, shorter after a change to a check lands or while findings cluster, longer while
  its modules are small: by default, after every fifth module it integrates. The rows are
  always read at each ship point and at an audit's end.

The record is committed on Crustify's working branch of the campaign and reaches `devel`
with it. Rows are appended in landing order and statuses edited in place, so that a merge
of two campaigns' working branches keeps both campaigns' rows, ordered by their landing.
Under `propose`, where no rule changes, the readings still run and their statuses are
committed all the same, since a record commit changes no rule, and they are put to the user
with the campaign's proposals. Under `off`, they do not run.

## 2. Evolving evolution

Evolution evolves from its own record, as everything else does from a campaign's. At a
campaign's end the record and the campaign's proposals are read for what repeats: changes
that recurred; changes the review rejected or the user declined, by cause; signals a run
met that no proposal answered; how long a blocking defect held its run; and what the
reviews bought for what they cost: per change, the findings each round made that held, those
its author's own validation had already caught, the rounds it took and their cost. How deep
a review reads, and how many rounds a kind of change gets, follow from that evidence, not
from a fixed rule. Each is a
signal of this guidance, as [`evolution`](../SKILL.md)'s Signals section lists them, and its proposal is on this
skill, on the agents' evolution rules or on what the review checks.

- **Measure.** Of what a campaign's evidence taught, the share stated as rules without the
  target's names against the share kept as the target's lessons. Also the rules a second
  target could not follow as written.

## 10. Least constraint

A rule states what must hold. Unless the how is itself what must hold, the rule leaves the
how to the agent.

- **Measure.** Per module, the rules that a run:
  - worked around;
  - rewrote sound code to satisfy; or
  - reported as forcing a worse result.
- **Paired with** what a loosened rule let through: the changes marked as weakening a check,
  and the defects found where a rule was loosened.

## 11. Consistency

One kind of item is translated one way. Items that mean the same in C take the same Rust
pattern, whatever their syntax and whichever agent, batch or campaign translates them. The
pattern is the one the conventions and the how-to skills give them. A departure states its
reason.

A pattern a skill gives is a how that must hold, in Least constraint's terms. A pattern is
given only where translating the same thing two ways costs a consumer or a reviewer. Where
the skills give none, the agent chooses. A choice met twice, where two ways would cost, is
proposed as the pattern rather than left to converge.

- **Measure.** The conventions findings reviews file, per item.
- **Paired with** two measures, since a review that reads less finds less:
  - the items a later batch or review reshaped; and
  - the conventions findings a later tier makes on an item an earlier review passed.
- **Not taken yet.**
  - both paired measures;
  - the departures that state their reason, against the departures a review had to find; and
  - whether an item translated twice took the same shape both times.

## 12. Attribution

Every fact a decision rests on can be reproduced. Every change traces back to the run, and
the revisions, that made it.

- **Measure.** The landed commits, dashboard cells and decisions that trace to a run, its
  session and its revisions, against those that do not. Two examples of those that do not: a
  run without a recorded session, and a figure no rerun of its tool reproduces.
## 1. Record

Every change that lands is recorded in Crustify's own repository, in
[`EVOLUTION.md`](../../../../EVOLUTION.md), whatever component it changed, so that a later
campaign can tell whether it held. A row gives the campaign and proposal the change came
from, the component and commit it landed as, the signal it answered, its recurrence signal
and its status, with a change that weakens a check marked so in its status. A change no
proposal filed names its campaign and `no proposal` in its place, with where it came from.
A proposal that lands several changes takes a row for each.

A change's row is drafted in its proposal, so that the review reads it. The record's writer
copies the row into the record when the change lands. An evolution branch never edits
`EVOLUTION.md`, so that two changes awaiting review never conflict there, and the record
has one writer per campaign. The record holds every change landed since it began, on
2026-11-12; what landed before is not recorded.

The recurrence signal is what a campaign would observe if the issue were back, in what a
campaign produces anyway: a review finding of a category, a run that fails for a cause, a
tool's error, a correction the user repeats. A change whose regression test checks all of
it has `test` in its place and is not watched. One with no signal a campaign could observe
has `none`, with why, and is not watched either.

A watched change is:

- `watched` from its landing;
- `recurred` once its signal is met again, with the evidence, which opens a proposal that
  cites the row: the change was wrong or partial, or the validation and review that passed
  it were; and
- `confirmed` once a campaign other than the one it came from has ended, having exercised
  it, without the signal.

A row's signal is looked for at two times, in every campaign:

- when a proposal is indexed, as [`evolution`](../SKILL.md)'s Proposals section describes:
  a signal that matches a row's recurrence signal marks that row `recurred`; and
- periodically, when the rows still `watched` are read against the findings, failed runs,
  proposals and corrections since the last reading. The campaign sets the period from its
  state, shorter after a change to a check lands or while findings cluster, longer while
  its modules are small: by default, after every fifth module it integrates. The rows are
  always read at each ship point and at an audit's end.

The record is committed on Crustify's working branch of the campaign and reaches `devel`
with it. Rows are appended in landing order and statuses edited in place, so that a merge
of two campaigns' working branches keeps both campaigns' rows, ordered by their landing.
Under `propose`, where no rule changes, the readings still run and their statuses are
committed all the same, since a record commit changes no rule, and they are put to the user
with the campaign's proposals. Under `off`, they do not run.

## 2. Evolving evolution

Evolution evolves from its own record, as everything else does from a campaign's. At a
campaign's end the record and the campaign's proposals are read for what repeats: changes
that recurred; changes the review rejected or the user declined, by cause; signals a run
met that no proposal answered; how long a blocking defect held its run; and what the
reviews bought for what they cost: per change, the findings each round made that held, those
its author's own validation had already caught, the rounds it took and their cost. How deep
a review reads, and how many rounds a kind of change gets, follow from that evidence, not
from a fixed rule. Each is a
signal of this guidance, as [`evolution`](../SKILL.md)'s Signals section lists them, and its proposal is on this
skill, on the agents' evolution rules or on what the review checks.

A campaign evolves each component, Crustify or a tool, on a working branch of its own in
that component's repository, `<campaign-id>/devel`, the campaign id being the name of the
campaign's repository. It is forked from the component's `devel` when the campaign first
needs it, and the campaign's runs read and run the component from its checkout, so that a
campaign runs on what it has changed and no other campaign does.

A change is made on a branch named `<campaign-id>/evolution/<slug>`, forked from that
working branch, in a worktree beside the repository that lives only while the change is
made. A branch holds one concern. Once the change lands on the working branch, by a
fast-forward, the worktree is purged and the branch deleted. Its commits take the identity
[`versioning`](../../operations/versioning/SKILL.md)'s Identity section gives the
campaign's.

- A change to the spec follows `authoring`: written once, in the place its kind belongs,
  as generally as the evidence allows.
- A change to what a tool does comes with a regression test: the reproducer of a defect
  becomes one, and a new behaviour gets one that fails without it. A change to its
  documentation alone adds none, unless the defect it fixes has a reproducer, which becomes
  a test or a doctest. A packaging defect's reproducer becomes a test too, run
  against a build installed as a dependent installs it. The tool's whole suite passes, its
  opt-in tests included wherever the change touches what they cover.
- A new tool is drafted and tested where it serves a repeated procedure, preferably as a
  subcommand of an existing tool within that tool's goals, or as a script in the skill
  that describes its use, as `authoring` places one; a tool of its own repository is
  merged upstream only with the user's approval.

A fix that unblocks the campaign, or that would prevent a defect in later campaigns, is
landed on the working branch as soon as it is reviewed, rather than batched.

## 7. Validation

A tool's change is validated by its tests, the regression test it adds among them.

A spec change that a failure prompted is validated by running again what failed, the item,
the batch or the stage, under the change: a lightweight run, without the tests or gates
the failure does not need to show. The proposal records what the run produced before and
after, and a change whose rerun still fails does not land. A spec change no failure
prompted, such as a rule loosened or a waste removed, is validated the same way where its
effect is in doubt, on the item its evidence came from.

A rerun shows that a change answers the case that exposed it, not that it holds: that is
watched in the campaigns after it lands, as [`evolution-record`](record/SKILL.md) describes.

## 9. Autonomy

mkdir -p /target/libgit2-crustify/crustify/.worktrees/modules/libgit2/src/util/integer.h/wave-223/batch-0/crustify/evolution/config-branches-the-target-never-builds && cat > /target/libgit2-crustify/crustify/.worktrees/modules/libgit2/src/util/integer.h/wave-223/batch-0/crustify/evolution/config-branches-the-target-never-builds/PROPOSAL.md <<'EOF'
# A macro's branches for compilers and platforms the crate never targets do not shim it

Status: `open`.

Goal: Idiomatic Rust, and Least constraint: a shim over a branch the crate cannot be built
in constrains the port without a reason. Fitness: the rules a run worked around, per module
(Least constraint's measure), here one task message's override.

## Signal

A rule an agent works around, met as the recurrence signal of the record's row
`config-branches-of-one-result` (crustify `769d102`, `watched`): "a task message ... that
settles again whether a configuration-dependent macro is ported or shimmed".

## Evidence

`wave-223/batch-0/run-1` ported `src/util/integer.h`'s six overflow macros. The header
chooses each by compiler: clang's and gcc's `__builtin_*_overflow` intrinsics, Microsoft's
`<intsafe.h>` functions under `_MSC_VER`, and `GIT_INLINE` fallbacks for a compiler with
neither; `git__multiply_int64_overflow` also takes its fallback under clang on a 32-bit
target (`GIT_ARCH_32`). Five of the six compute one result in every branch, as the record's
row has it. The sixth does not: the fallback of `git__multiply_int64_overflow` reports
`INT64_MIN * -1` and `-1 * INT64_MIN` as fitting and `INT64_MIN * 1` and `1 * INT64_MIN` as
overflowing, the opposite of the intrinsic, and `tests/util/integer.c`'s edge-case test
asserts the fallback's answers (its body compiles empty on every variant, which defines the
macro as the intrinsic).

`porting-symbols`' Macros section, as `config-branches-of-one-result` landed it, says: "Only
one whose branches differ in what they compute keeps the shim `binding-symbols` gives it".
Read literally, `git__multiply_int64_overflow` would be bound through
`crustify_git__multiply_int64_overflow` rather than ported, though no build of the crate can
take the branch that differs: the bindings are generated for the host target alone and
`src/sys.rs` fails to compile on any other (`bindgen`'s Generation section), every variant
compiles the C with clang for x86-64 (`crustify/artifacts/build.json`), and the bundled build
uses the `plain` variant's configuration. The task message had to settle it again: "Where the
header has several configured branches, port what this build defines, as porting-symbols'
Macros section and strnlen_h.rs do." The batch ported `checked_mul_i64` over `i64::checked_mul`
and recorded the fallback's four inputs in the module's docs and in a carried-over unit test.

The section does not say which configurations its exception means. A configuration the crate
can be built in, a build option such as the SHA-1 backend or threads, which a dependent's
bundled build could select, is one a port must answer for; a compiler or a platform the crate

set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"

"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
import subprocess,sys,pathlib,json,glob,os
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'
    subprocess.run([B+'llvm-profdata','merge','-sparse','-o',str(prof)]+raws,check=True)
    return prof
def total(prof,srcs):
    cd=[]
    if srcs==['@c']: use,srcs=cobjs,[]
    else:
        use=objs
        if '@' in srcs[-1]: srcs[-1],c=srcs[-1].split('@'); cd=['-compilation-dir='+c]
    args=[B+'llvm-cov','report','-instr-profile',str(prof)]+cd+[use[0]]+sum((['-object',o] for o in use[1:]),[])+srcs
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.returncode: sys.exit(r.stderr[-2000:])
    lines=r.stdout.splitlines()
    if srcs and not cd:
        roots=[str(pathlib.Path(d).resolve()) for d in srcs]
        rows=[l.split()[0] for l in lines[2:] if l.strip() and not l.startswith(('-','TOTAL','Filename'))]
        stray=[f for f in rows if not any(str(pathlib.Path(f).resolve()).startswith(r+'/') or str(pathlib.Path(f).resolve())==r for r in roots)]
        if stray: sys.exit(f'scope {srcs} reports {len(stray)} files outside it, such as {stray[0]}: its filters match no source')
    t=[l for l in lines if l.startswith('TOTAL')][-1].split()
    # TOTAL regions missed cover functions missed exec lines missed cover branches missed cover
    return dict(lines=(int(t[7])-int(t[8]),int(t[7]),t[9]),functions=(int(t[4])-int(t[5]),int(t[4]),t[6]),regions=(int(t[1])-int(t[2]),int(t[1]),t[3]))
res={}
skip=os.environ.get('MERGED')
four=[x for x in suites if x!='doc']
only=os.environ.get('ONLY')
for s in ([only] if only else suites+['TOTAL','ALL']):
    prof=out/f'{s}.profdata' if skip else merge(s,four if s=='TOTAL' else suites if s=='ALL' else [s])
    res[s]={n:total(prof,src.split(':')) for n,src in scopes.items()}
    print(s,json.dumps(res[s]))
(out/(f'figures-{only}.json' if only else 'figures.json')).write_text(json.dumps(res,indent=1))

# The packaging gate's procedure, for a crate whose dependencies are unpublished

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A procedure worked out by hand that a skill should state: `testing-gates`' Regressions
section says that a batch that changes the raw bindings packages the safe crate, "built
alone in bundled mode from the C it packages, with no build variant selected", and that
"each crate the package depends on is patched to its local source", but not how. The
direct form fails, and the steps that pass were found by trial.

## Evidence

`wave-229/batch-0/run-1` (`src/util/utf8.c`, which allowlists three functions), on base
`2216b0cd0`, the first packaging gate since the tree's change of 2026-11-13:

1. `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= cargo package --offline --allow-dirty` stops before verifying:
   `no matching package named glibc-bindings found` (crates.io index). The packaged
   manifest drops the Git source of `glibc-bindings` and the path of `ffibox`, keeping
   their versions, and the workspace's `[patch]` tables, keyed by those sources, do not
   apply to it.
2. `cargo package --offline --allow-dirty --no-verify --exclude-lockfile` packages (697
   files). Extracted under `crustify/tmp/`, the package's manifest needs an empty
   `[workspace]`, since the worktree's own encloses it, and
   `[patch.crates-io] glibc-bindings = { path = "/target/glibc-crustify" }` and
   `ffibox = { path = "/crustify-rs/ffibox" }`.
3. `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= cargo build --offline` there then fails in CMake: PCRE2, then
   zlib, not found. The host has neither: the bundled build finds them only through the
   side campaigns' `plain` installs, `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR` and `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, the
   latter `:`-separated in the environment where `build.json`'s `-D` form takes `;`.
   With `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=<openssl install>` and
   `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<openssl install>:<pcre2 install>:<zlib install>`, the package
   builds alone: cmake builds `libgit2.a` and `libcrustify_git2.a` into `OUT_DIR`.

`modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1` (the switch of `src/cli/opt.c`, on
`f68ea8660`), the next packaging gate, followed steps 2 and 3 and failed to compile the
package's `lib`: two copies of ffibox, `0.1.1` by path for the crate and `0.1.0` by Git
(`40621a2`) for `glibc-bindings`, whose manifest takes ffibox by Git. The workspace patches
that Git source too (`[patch."https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffibox"]`), and step 2's
`[patch.crates-io]` does not stand for it. `opt.rs`'s gateway, which compiles from this switch
on, is the first code of the crate to pass a `glibc_bindings` `FileRef` through the crate's
own ffibox traits (`FileRef::from_ptr`, E0599 four times), so `utf8.c`'s gate could not have
met it. With the workspace's Git patch copied into the package's manifest as well, and the
lockfile the first attempt wrote removed, so that the patch applies, the graph holds one
ffibox and the package builds alone (696 files). Its `lib` tests: 829 pass and 58 fail, the
58 needing `c/tests/resources`, as at `utf8.c`'s gate. So the script copies every `[patch]`
table of the workspace, the Git sources' as well as crates.io's, and resolves with no
lockfile.

## Destination

The spec: `testing-gates`' Regressions section, with a script beside it, as `authoring`
places a procedure that must run exactly so, documented by its `--help`: it packages
without verifying, patches each unpublished dependency to the source the workspace's
`[patch]` names for it, gives the extracted package a workspace of its own, puts the
out-of-tree libraries' installs of the `plain` variant on the build system's search paths,
and builds it with no variant, in a scratch dir it removes.

## Change

Not made: the gate is not a translator's to change. The section would name the script,
and say that the patches and search paths stand in for what a dependent's host supplies.

content.content:
### Overview test counts

The Coverage stats test lines were measured again on 2026-11-04, at `crustify/devel`
`1e732ebff`, with the testing spec's Coverage method, which replaces the gcov one the
earlier figures used. Those figures are not comparable with these. Each count is the
number of tests its compiled test binary registers (`-- --list`): `--lib` for the unit
tests, one of them ignored, and the `ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe` and `equiv` integration crates.
The trybuild runner is one `ub_safe` test, and it was skipped in the coverage run since it
runs no code. `ub_safe` holds 688 tests since the unsafe fixtures were removed. Doctests
are not counted in the table.

The `coverage` variant, `build.json` version 4, and the side libraries' `coverage`
installs (version 3 of each) compile the C with clang 23,
`-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping`. The Rust is a scratch copy under
`crustify/tmp/coverage/` with `#[coverage(off)]` on every test item, compiled on
`nightly-2026-10-08` (LLVM 23) with `-C instrument-coverage`. Each suite ran alone into
its own profile, and `Total tests` is the merge of the four suites' profiles, their union.
Every figure is the `TOTAL` line of the nightly's `llvm-cov report`, with `libgit2.so` and
every test binary as objects for every suite.

- C is line coverage over the 86,770 lines `libgit2.so` maps to `c/src/libgit2`,
  `c/src/util`, `c/include` and the bundled `c/deps` it compiles (`llhttp`, `ntlmclient`,
  `reftable`, `xdiff`). The generated headers and the C's own tests count toward none.
  libgit2 proper, `src/` and `include/` without `deps/`, is `52.42`% of 68,023 lines. The
  total covers `61.63`% of functions and `47.65`% of regions.
- Rust is line coverage over the 13,226 lines of the crate's 42 files under `src/`, with

## Safety audit

Deterministic `ffimap`, run as the `ffimap` skill's Accounting section describes; no
model. Every counter is in the `ffimap.json` tracked in the campaign's artifact dir, in
each wave's `waves/wave-<index>/` and in each batch run's dir. Each metric is one counter
or a combination of counters, named by their dotted paths into the scan's `counts`; a `%`
metric is a share within one record, and a `−` subtracts a share from the record it cuts.

### Metrics

| metric | counters | what it counts |
|---|---|---|
| pub raw ptr | `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` | raw pointers a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`: public fields and the signatures of safe public fns; target 0 |
| pub void ptr | `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` | type-erased pointers left to the API's users, `unsafe fn`s included |
| pub unsafe fn | `fn.unsafe.pub` | the obligations the crate exports to its callers |
| &cell | `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub` | public references to a cell outside the positions ffibox sanctions, where the convention wants a handle; target 0 |
| C by value | `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total` + `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total` | C structs held by value or in a standard-library owner rather than through a cell, which a move can leave dangling |
| celled % | `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` / `….of_which.used` | of the C types the bindings pass by pointer that the crate uses, those a cell covers |
| raw→std | `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.total` | raw pointers turned into a standard-library borrow, slice, string or owner, whose lifetime or ownership the type system then trusts |
| unmanaged ptr types | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total` | types that store a raw pointer and declare nothing about it |
| ptr Drop | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total` | types that store a raw pointer and free it by hand, rather than through an owner |
| Send/Sync | `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total` + `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total` | thread safety asserted rather than derived from the fields |
| raw deref | `raw_ptr.deref.total` | raw-pointer reads and writes in bodies, each a pointer the code vouches for |
| FFI calls | `code.unsafe_call.ffi` | calls across the C boundary, through bindings or stored function pointers |
| unsafe loc % | `code.loc.unsafe` / `code.loc.total` | lines of unsafe code over code lines; the comparable measure of unsafe volume |
| unsafe blocks | `code.unsafe_block.total` − `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` | hand-written unsafe blocks, a port's generated export gateways left out; moves with the one-op-per-block policy, so not comparable across crates |

import json
def load(p): return json.load(open(p))
b,t=load('ffimap-base.json'),load('ffimap-tree.json')
def g(d,path):
    o=d['counts']
    for k in path.split('.'): o=o[k]
    return o
def m(d):
    r={}
    r['pub raw ptr']=g(d,'raw_ptr.total.safe.pub')
    r['pub void ptr']=g(d,'raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub')+sum(g(d,f'raw_ptr.{a}.of_which.void.{s}.pub') for a in ['fn_sig_arg','fn_sig_ret'] for s in ['safe','unsafe'])
    r['pub unsafe fn']=g(d,'fn.unsafe.pub')
    w='ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std'
    r['&cell']=g(d,w+'.pub')-g(d,w+'.of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub')-g(d,w+'.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub')
    r['C by value']=g(d,'ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total')+g(d,'ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total')
    x='ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which'
    r['celled %']=g(d,x+'.wrapped')/g(d,x+'.used')*100
    r['raw→std']=g(d,'raw_ptr.casted_to.std.total')
    r['unmanaged']=g(d,'ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total')
    r['ptr Drop']=g(d,'ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total')
    r['Send/Sync']=g(d,'ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total')+g(d,'ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total')
    r['raw deref']=g(d,'raw_ptr.deref.total')
    r['FFI calls']=g(d,'code.unsafe_call.ffi')
    r['unsafe loc %']=g(d,'code.loc.unsafe')/g(d,'code.loc.total')*100
    r['unsafe blocks']=g(d,'code.unsafe_block.total')-g(d,'code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export')
    r['loc']=g(d,'code.loc.total'); r['tests loc']=g(d,'code.tests.loc.total')
    r['sys fns']=g(d,'fn.ffibox.sys.total'); r['sys used']=g(d,'fn.ffibox.sys.of_which.used')
    return r
mb,mt=m(b),m(t)

### `libgit2/src/util/integer.h` wave 223 batch 0: the range checks and overflow checks

`src/util/integer.h` is a header with no translation unit. Its six `GIT_INLINE` range checks
and six overflow macros are native Rust in `src/libgit2/src/util/integer_h.rs`, which holds no
unsafe region and carries `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`: `fits_usize`, `fits_isize`, `fits_u16`,
`fits_u32`, `fits_c_ulong` and `fits_c_int`, generic over `TryInto<T>`, and the `const fn`s
`checked_add_usize`, `checked_mul_usize`, `checked_add_c_int`, `checked_sub_c_int`,
`checked_add_i64` and `checked_mul_i64`, over the standard library's `checked_*`, each
`None` on overflow. No C reaches them and none is exported: the header stays, whole, for the
C that includes it (`git2_util.h`, every TU, and `vector.c`). On this build, clang for x86-64
in every variant, the macros are the `__builtin_*_overflow` intrinsics; the module's docs name
the `<intsafe.h>` and `GIT_INLINE` branches, and the four inputs on which
`git__multiply_int64_overflow`'s fallback, taken only without intrinsics or under clang on a
32-bit target, answers otherwise. The `loc` cell is wavefront's `query dag --loc`, `4` per
function and `0` per macro; `+LoC` counts the hand-written Rust, the generated bindings
(`+30`) and C wrappers (`+6`) left out.

Deliberate departures, documented and held by tests: C's round trips keep values the ranges
do not hold, and the ports refuse them. `git__is_ssizet` never returns false (a `size_t` to
`ssize_t` and back keeps every value), so `p_read`'s and `git_futils_readbuffer_fd`'s guards
accept a count past `SSIZE_MAX`; `fits_isize` refuses it. `git__is_sizet` and `git__is_ulong`
accept every negative `int64_t` on this 64-bit build, as `pack-objects.c`'s `config_get` of
`pack.deltaCacheSize` does before converting it to `size_t`; `fits_usize` and `fits_c_ulong`
refuse them, and for a `uint64_t` a C caller passes through the parameter they give C's
answer at its own type. Where C stores the intrinsic's wrapped result on overflow
(`try_delta`'s `delta_cache_size`), the ports return nothing; the branches disagree there.

Tests: twelve `unit_pub` tests, which carry over all three cases of `tests/util/integer.c`
(81 products that fit with their values, 63 that overflow, and the four edge cases at this
build's answers, the C case asserting the fallback's) and the inputs of
`tests/util/errors.c`'s `test_errors__integer_overflow_sets_oom`, and check each operation
against `i128` arithmetic over its bounds, the range checks at theirs, and the chain
`patch_parse.c`'s `parse_hunk_body` computes; twelve doctests; and seven `equiv` tests. The
range checks are compared through their raw bindings, the six allowlisted `static inline`
functions `static_fns.c` now wraps (they go with the equivalence tests at the switch), the C's
departures asserted beside the ports' refusals. The macros are compared where they expand:
`git__multiply_sizet_overflow` in `git__calloc`, `git__mallocarray` and `git__reallocarray`;
`git__add_sizet_overflow` in `git_strlist_copy_with_null`; and `git__multiply_int64_overflow`
and `git__add_int64_overflow` in `git_config_parse_int64` and its `git__strntol64`, over signs,
bases and unit suffixes at each bound. `git__add_int_overflow` and `git__sub_int_overflow`
expand only in `parse_hunk_body`, which no raw binding reaches: unreached, checked by the unit
test at its arguments. No C test is tied to the module in `modules.json`; `tests/util/integer.c`
compiles empty on every variant and none of its cases is left uncarried.

Coverage was measured with `crustify/scripts/coverage/run.sh` on a `git archive` of the wave
tip `2d68a9f28` and on this tree, each suite alone, and read with `report.py` from each
scratch tree's `src/libgit2` (`C=@c` over the `coverage` variant's `libcrustify.a`, 88,226
lines; Rust over the scratch tree's `src/`), the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`.
The tip's counts were `equiv` 532 and `unit_pub` 241, where the Coverage stats recorded 538
and 1140 for an earlier tree. The C shifts of suites this batch does not change (`ub_safe`
`+0.01`, `ub_unsafe` `-0.03` pp) and the `equiv` C `-0.02` pp are run-to-run variation.
Worklist: Rust `integer_h.rs` 36 of 36 lines, 36 of 36 regions, 12 of 12 functions; C
`integer.h`'s copies in the archive 4 of 6 functions (`git__is_uint32` and `git__is_ulong`
unreached by any suite, their callers in diff, delta and pack code), the same as on the tip,
since the wrappers the `equiv` tests call are compiled into the crate, outside the archive.
The Overview's Rust LoC moves by ffimap's `code.loc.total` (`+37`) and `code.tests.loc.total`
(`+632`).

The safety audit scans (ffimap `50a800e`, `--ffibox`, `--sys-crates crate::sys,pcre2_sys`,
the 13 seams, `--regions ffi_import,ffi_export`, no export feature) move only `unsafe loc %`,
by the new safe lines, and the six bindings in `fn.ffibox.sys.total`; the boundary scan's
sites are unchanged, none in the changeset. `ffimap api` against the tip, with ffibox's
private rustdoc JSON (nightly `2026-10-08`): the twelve items are `new`, every unattributed
module `kept` but `sys::libgit2`, `extended` by the six bindings.

Gates, on the base `2d68a9f28`: the workspace is formatted (nightly), and `clippy
--all-targets` passes with warnings denied. The whole workspace passes on `plain` (`lib` 907
and 1 ignored, `ub_safe` 798, `ub_unsafe` 144, `equiv` 539, `unit_pub` 253, `hidden_symbols` 1,
doctests 118 merged and 397 standalone) and under ASan+UBSan. Miri passes the twelve unit
tests, the twelve doctests and the one `equiv` test that calls no C; the six others were each
run alone there and stop at `git_libgit2_init` or at a `git__is_*__extern` wrapper. TSan and
BSan have no obligation: no unsafe code, no `Send` or `Sync` claim, no thread. The raw
bindings changed, so the crate was packaged (`--no-verify --exclude-lockfile`, 701 files) and
built alone in bundled mode with no variant, as `package-gate-procedure` records, its archive
holding the six wrappers. Proposal: `config-branches-the-target-never-builds`
(`porting-symbols`), meeting `config-branches-of-one-result`'s recurrence signal. Usage cells
are the assistant's.

content.text:
Wave 223 batch 0 has landed: `9b43c913d` is on `refs/heads/crustify/waves/wave-223`. All twelve items of `src/util/integer.h` are ported, and nothing is blocked.

**What was ported** (`src/libgit2/src/util/integer_h.rs`)
- The module has no unsafe code (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`) and no exports. Remaining C still uses its own copy of the header (`git2_util.h`, which every file includes, and `vector.c`); the module docs say so.
- **The six range checks** are `fits_usize`, `fits_isize`, `fits_u16`, `fits_u32`, `fits_c_ulong` and `fits_c_int`. Each is generic over `TryInto` because the C callers pass signed and unsigned 64-bit values through the same `int64_t` parameter.
- **The six overflow macros** are `const fn`s over the standard library's `checked_*` operations, returning `None` on overflow. This build compiles them to clang's `__builtin_*_overflow` intrinsics. The docs describe the other two branches (MSVC's `<intsafe.h>` and the plain-C fallback). The fallback of `git__multiply_int64_overflow` gives a different answer on four inputs; the port follows this build.

**Choices for you to check**
1. **Three C bugs are not copied.**
   - `git__is_ssizet` can never return false, so the guards in `p_read` and `git_futils_readbuffer_fd` never fire.
   - On this 64-bit build, `git__is_sizet` and `git__is_ulong` accept negative values.
   - The ports reject these out-of-range values. Each departure is documented and tested, and the equivalence tests confirm the C really does behave this way.
2. **Nothing is returned on overflow.** The C intrinsics write a wrapped result even when they report overflow. One caller relies on it: `try_delta` in `pack-objects.c` leaves the wrapped sum in `delta_cache_size`. The three C branches leave different values there, so the ports return `None` instead.
3. **Six new raw bindings.** I allowlisted the six `git__is_*` functions, so `static_fns.c` now wraps them. Only the equivalence tests use them, and the allowlist comment says they go at the switch.
4. **The `+LoC` cell counts hand-written Rust only (+1124).** It leaves out the generated bindings (+30) and the C wrappers (+6).

**Tests**
- 12 `unit_pub` tests, 12 doctests and 7 equivalence tests.
- The macros are compared with the C where it expands them: `git__calloc`, `git__mallocarray`, `git__reallocarray`, `git_strlist_copy_with_null` and `git_config_parse_int64`.
- `git__add_int_overflow` and `git__sub_int_overflow` expand only in `patch_parse.c`, which no binding reaches. They are not compared with C; a unit test checks them at that call site's arguments.
- **C test cases not carried over by any `unit_pub` test: none.** All three cases of `tests/util/integer.c` are carried over; their bodies compile empty on every variant here. For `test_integer__multiply_int64_edge_cases`, the four expected results are this build's answers, the opposite of what the C asserts for the fallback. I also carried over the inputs of `test_errors__integer_overflow_sets_oom`.

**Gates** (on the base `2d68a9f28`)
- Format (nightly) and `clippy --all-targets` with warnings denied pass.
- The whole workspace passes on `plain` and under ASan+UBSan.
- Miri passes all the Rust-only tests. Each of the six tests marked to skip under Miri was run alone and stops at a C call.
- The packaging gate passed (701 files, built alone in bundled mode), since the bindings changed.
- TSan and BSan were not needed: no unsafe code, no `Send`/`Sync` claims, no threads.
- **After the rebase I reran no gate.** The wave branch was still at my base, so the rebase did nothing and the landed tree is the one the gates ran on.

**Dashboard**: I filled the landing cells only (Overview LoC, Coverage stats, four Symbols tables with their Σ rows, and a Notes entry). The usage cells are left for you.

**Evolution**: I filed one proposal, `crustify/evolution/config-branches-the-target-never-builds`, on the Macros section of `porting-symbols`.
- **The problem:** as written, that section would require a shim for `git__multiply_int64_overflow`, even though no build of the crate can take the branch that differs. Your task message had to settle it again.
- **Why a new proposal:** this meets the recurrence signal of the `config-branches-of-one-result` row in `EVOLUTION.md`, so that row should be marked `recurred`.
- **To do:** it needs a row in `INDEX.md`.

I deleted the scratch builds under `crustify/tmp/` (about 4.7 GB). The worktree's own `target/` (3.5 GB) is left for the purge.
